userStories.title: Configure review limits and separate branch coverage retries
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add review defaults and connect the branch op to independent coverage retries with progress prompts.

**Motivation** — The log line said `JSON parse retry — invalid shape`, although the reply had parsed.

**Approach** — **Config.** `WorkflowConfigObjectSchema` gains:
```ts
review: z.object({
  sliceFiles: z.number().int().min(1).default(15),
  coverageRetries: z.number().int().min(0).default(3),
}).prefault({}),
```
`runtime-types-workflow.ts` `WorkflowConfig` gains `review?: { readonly sliceFiles: number; readonly coverageRetries: number }` (optional, so hand-built test configs keep compiling). `schemas-workflow.ts` exports `WORKFLOW_REVIEW_DEFAULTS`, the parsed defaults of the `review` object, and consumers read `workflow.review ?? WORKFLOW_REVIEW_DEFAULTS`, imported from `@/config` (the barrel `src/config/index.ts` lists it beside `WORKFLOW_DEFAULTS`). `FIELD_DESCRIPTIONS` in `src/cli/config-descriptions.ts` gains non-empty rows for `workflow.review`, `workflow.review.sliceFiles` and `workflow.review.coverageRetries`.

**Branch op.** `workflowBranchReviewOp.retry` becomes `makeCoverageRetryStrategy` over a `makeParseRetryStrategy` with `maxAttempts: 2`, whose `validate` is only `parsed !== null` and whose `invalid` prompt is `buildWorkflowReviewJsonRetry()`. `missing` is `unreadFiles(input.requiredFiles, verdict.inspectedFiles, input.repoRoot)`. `maxCoverageRetries` is `input.coverageRetries`, or `WORKFLOW_REVIEW_DEFAULTS.coverageRetries` when absent. `prompt` is `buildWorkflowBranchCoverageRetry(input.range, missing, false, progress)`.

`buildWorkflowBranchCoverageRetry(range, missing, staticMode = false, progress?)` gains the optional `progress: { attempt: number; max: number }`. With it, the retry adds `This is coverage retry <attempt> of <max>. Read all of them before you reply; a file you leave out stays unread and keeps the PR a draft.`

The ruled exception in `.nax/rules/retry-strategy.md` (coverage inside the strategy, not in `op.parse`) still holds after this change: coverage only decides whether to ask again, and an incomplete verdict is kept. Its wording names `validate`, which no longer carries coverage; the rule text update is a manual step (Out of Scope).

Update test/unit/config/workflow-config.test.ts: its defaults test asserts parsed.workflow with toEqual against an object that has no review key. Add review: { sliceFiles: 15, coverageRetries: 3 }; every other member keeps its value. Update test/unit/operations/workflow-branch-review.test.ts AC-11 from attempt-1 shared-budget exhaustion to no-progress exhaustion with fallback equal to parseBranchReviewReply(lastOutput, []), findings included. The unparseable-reply assertions (AC-12 and the JSON prompt) hold unchanged. Add the two new unit files listed in expectedFiles; exercise two successive coverage retries through callOp with a stub agent as well.

**Scope** — In: schema/runtime type/config barrel/descriptions, branch-op wrapper, optional progress text, and compatibility assertion updates. Out: bot wrapper (US-003), initial required-file prompt section (US-004), slice orchestration (US-008), and manual rule text changes.

**Interface** —
```ts
// WorkflowBranchReviewInput adds:
readonly coverageRetries?: number;
// WorkflowConfig adds:
review?: { readonly sliceFiles: number; readonly coverageRetries: number };
// Target prompt signature:
(range: string, missing: readonly string[], staticMode = false, progress?: { attempt: number; max: number }) => string
```

userStories.title: Give bot review independent coverage retries
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Apply the shared coverage retry budget to both bot review ops without changing triage precedence.

**Motivation** — `nax bot review` at `ec1c569` read 1 file, approved because "the settled rulings say the files were already read", spent its coverage re-prompt on ~60 files, diffed 4, and posted ~60 false "Not read by the review" lines.

**Approach** — **Bot ops.** `reviewRetry` in `bot-pr-review.ts` keeps its `makeParseRetryStrategy` with `maxAttempts: 2` and `validate` = triage complete only (the `missingFiles` term moves out), and its `invalid` prompt keeps the triage retry and drops the coverage branch. The wrapper adds coverage, with `missing` = `missingFiles(verdict)`, `maxCoverageRetries` = `input.coverageRetries` (default as above), and `prompt` = `buildWorkflowBranchCoverageRetry(coverage.range, missing, staticMode, progress)`. With no `requiredFiles`, `missing` is always empty. The existing `coverageContext` throw (`BOT_REVIEW_COVERAGE_INVALID` when non-empty `requiredFiles` is set without `repoRoot` or `range`) is kept.

`reviewRetry` in `src/operations/bot-pr-review.ts` as in Design § Approach; `BotPrReviewInput` gains `coverageRetries`; `runPrReview` passes `(ctx.workflow.review ?? WORKFLOW_REVIEW_DEFAULTS).coverageRetries`. The default above is WORKFLOW_REVIEW_DEFAULTS.coverageRetries (3). Stop on budget or no progress with the last parsed verdict, findings retained; an exhausted triage fallback stops before coverage.

Update test/unit/operations/bot-pr-review.test.ts: (1) an attempt-1 triage-complete partial reply with an uncovered file now retries if no coverage retry has been sent; assert fallback after a coverage retry that covered no more files instead, using op.parse(partial, value, ctx()). (2) The US-015 AC-1–5 nextPrompt comparison gains progress { attempt: 1, max: 3 } in buildWorkflowBranchCoverageRetry(value.range, ["src/a.ts"], op === botPrStaticReviewOp, progress). The triage assertions at attempt 1 and the triage-before-coverage ordering hold unchanged. Add test/unit/operations/bot-pr-review-coverage.test.ts, including runPrReview-to-callOp budget wiring.

**Scope** — In: trusted/static bot retry wrappers and budget input plumbing. Out: settled-file credit (US-012), bot prompt credit section (US-012), branch slicing (US-008), tool-observed bot reads, and bot slicing.

**Interface** —
```ts
// BotPrReviewInput adds:
readonly coverageRetries?: number;
```

[unit] For botPrStaticReviewOp, the same reply returns nextPrompt equal to buildWorkflowBranchCoverageRetry(range, ["src/a.ts"], true, { attempt: 1, max: 3 }).
[unit] For botPrReviewOp, a reply missing a thread id and a required file returns the buildBotTriageRetry prompt, not the coverage prompt.

[unit] For botPrReviewOp at attempt 1, after one coverage retry, a triage-complete reply still missing src/a.ts with coverageRetries: 3 and no fewer missing files than before returns { retry: false, fallback: op.parse(lastOutput, input, ctx) }.
[unit] For botPrReviewOp at attempt 1 with no coverage retry sent, a reply still missing a thread id returns { retry: false } with the parsed fallback, as before.
[unit] For botPrReviewOp with no requiredFiles, a triage-complete reply returns { retry: false }.
[unit] For botPrReviewOp at attempt 1, a reply still missing a thread id and also missing src/a.ts returns { retry: false } with the parsed fallback and no coverage prompt.
[unit] botPrReviewOp.retry with requiredFiles: ["src/a.ts"] set and no range throws a NaxError of code BOT_REVIEW_COVERAGE_INVALID.

(1) At attempt 1 a triage-complete reply with an uncovered file (`partial`) was expected to stop with `fallback: op.parse(partial, value, ctx())`; with no coverage retry sent it now retries with the coverage prompt, so assert instead that after a coverage retry that covered no more files the same reply stops with that fallback. (2) The US-015 AC-1–5 test compares nextPrompt with buildWorkflowBranchCoverageRetry(value.range, ["src/a.ts"], op === botPrStaticReviewOp); compare with the same call plus the progress argument { attempt: 1, max: 3 }. userStories.title: State the branch review's required-file obligation
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Tell each branch review exactly which files it must read and explain the draft consequence.

**Motivation** — The prompt never lists the required files, never gives their count, and never says nax checks the list or that an unread file keeps the PR a draft.

**Approach** — **Prompt.** `BranchReviewPromptInput` gains `requiredFiles?: readonly string[]` and `slice?: { index: number; count: number; otherFiles: number }`. With a non-empty `requiredFiles`, `buildWorkflowBranchReviewPrompt` adds a section after "## How to read the diff":
```
## Files you must review (N)
- path/one.ts
- path/two.ts
nax compares your inspectedFiles with this list. A file on it that you do not read or diff is reported unread, and an unread file keeps the PR a draft. Repo gates passing is not a review of a file, and neither is a story review: read each one.
```
With `slice` set it adds a line to that section: `This is review slice <index> of <count>. Other slices review the other <otherFiles> changed file(s); read any of them only to check a contract with your files.` `buildBranchPackageReadingNote` (shared with the bot review package) replaces its `No diff is inlined.` sentence with `This package holds no diff, only the commit list, the --stat summary and the changed-file names.`, which closes #2859 minor 2.

Keep the existing git diff range instruction and omit the new section for absent or empty requiredFiles. Add test/unit/prompts/workflow-branch-builder-coverage.test.ts; existing unrelated prompt behavior remains unchanged.

**Scope** — In: initial branch prompt input and required-file/slice section, shared package-reading note sentence. Out: coverage retry progress (US-002), actual slice execution (US-008), and settled-ruling prompt section (US-012).

**Interface** —
```ts
// BranchReviewPromptInput adds:
requiredFiles?: readonly string[];
slice?: { index: number; count: number; otherFiles: number };
```

userStories.title: Recognize files read through nax review tools
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Extract whole-file read/diff credit from successful bounded tool-call records.

**Motivation** — Turn 1 read the spec, listed the changed files, read 3 of them, and approved.

**Approach** — **Tool-observed reads.** New `packages/nax/src/workflow/review-tool-reads.ts`:

`toolReadPaths` keeps calls with `outcome === "ok"` whose `resultBytes` is at or below `TOOL_READ_CREDIT_MAX_BYTES` (exported, `40_000`, the size nax-agent's `MODEL_MAX_BYTES` lets the model see), and returns repo-relative paths, deduplicated, in first-appearance order. A larger result reached the model cut short, so its call credits nothing.

- `Read`: `input.path`, only when the call has neither `offset` nor `limit` (a ranged read did not show the whole file).
- `Git`: `input.subcommand === "diff"` with `input.nameOnly !== true`: each `input.paths` entry.
- `Bash`: `input.command` is split into segments on `;`, `&&` and newlines, and each segment is cut at its first `|`. A segment `cd <dir>` (no `$`) sets the directory for the later segments. A segment whose words begin `git diff` or `rtk git diff`, that contains a standalone `--`, and that has none of `--name-only`, `--name-status` or `--stat`, contributes each word after `--` that does not start with `-` and contains none of `$ * ? [`, joined to the current directory.
- A word wrapped in single or double quotes is unquoted first, and a word whose quotes do not close is dropped.
- Each path is normalised the way `unreadFiles` normalises an entry: an absolute path inside `repoRoot` becomes relative, a leading `./` is dropped, and a path outside `repoRoot` is dropped. The private `normalize` in `src/operations/workflow-review-coverage.ts` is exported as `normalizeReviewPath(entry, repoRoot): string | undefined` and reused, not duplicated.

Add test/unit/workflow/review-tool-reads.test.ts with ToolCallRecord fixtures. ToolCallRecord is imported from @nathapp/nax-agent; the agent package is context only, not modified. Preserve unreadFiles behavior while renaming its shared normalization.

**Scope** — In: pure read-path extraction and shared normalization export. Out: audit-file loading (US-006), branch integration (US-009), bot tool credit, ACP-owned tools, and credit for cat/sed/head/git show. The specified git-diff-before-pipe case still earns credit.

**Interface** —
```ts
export function toolReadPaths(calls: readonly ToolCallRecord[], repoRoot: string): string[];
export const TOOL_READ_CREDIT_MAX_BYTES = 40_000;
export function normalizeReviewPath(entry: string, repoRoot: string): string | undefined;
```

[unit] toolReadPaths for a Read call with outcome "denied" returns [].
[unit] toolReadPaths for a Read of "/repo/src/a.ts" with repoRoot "/repo" returns ["src/a.ts"].
[unit] toolReadPaths for a Read of "/other/x.ts" with repoRoot "/repo" returns [].

userStories.title: Run branch review as sequential fresh slices
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Prepare the branch once, review directory-grouped slices sequentially, and return one merged verdict.

**Motivation** — 58 files is more than one session takes on.

**Approach** — **`runBranchReview`, sliced.** In `src/workflow/branch-review.ts`:

1. Write the package and compute `requiredFiles` once, before any slice, with the same failure semantics `underReviewLimit` gives a package failure: a throw while `fc.runSignal` is aborted rethrows, any other throw returns `{ ran: false, why: "review package failed: <message>" }`. The rules and project-context appends stay in this step.
2. `slices = planReviewSlices(requiredFiles, review.sliceFiles)`.
3. For each slice in order, build the prompt with `requiredFiles: slice` and, when there is more than one slice, `slice: { index, count, otherFiles }`, where `otherFiles` is the number of required files outside this slice. Run it through `underReviewLimit(fc, noop, run)` so each slice has its own review timeout, and call `workflowBranchReviewOp` with `requiredFiles: slice` and `coverageRetries: review.coverageRetries`. A slice that does not run records its `why` and the next slice still runs. An abort rethrows and stops the loop.
5. `merged = mergeSliceVerdicts(results)`. `null` returns `{ ran: false, why: <first slice's why> }`.
6. `unread = unreadFiles(requiredFiles, [...(merged.inspectedFiles ?? []), ...toolReads], fc.projectDir)`.
7. Return `merged`, plus `unreadFiles` when non-empty. `slices` is kept only when there was more than one slice, so a one-slice verdict is unchanged in shape.
